findings.where: d-a2-register (register wall) and the docked rail in every d-* shot (d-ch0, d-a6-sum, d-a6-ledger...)
findings.what: The black summary bar labeled NO YEAR OFF, 1921 TO 1970 is drawn spanning 1921 to 2026. On the wall the bar runs from the 1921 x-position to the 2026 axis end (1970 falls far short of the bar's right end), and the docked rail repeats the same overlong bar on every view. The ink contradicts its own label by 56 years.
findings.why: This is the exhibit's central quantitative claim, and drawn-versus-stated honesty is the show's whole covenant (real data only, every layer names its source). A visitor who reads the bar instead of the chip takes away the wrong number on every single screen.
findings.fix: End the black bar at the 1970 tick. If the intent is that some instrument (urban renewal) runs to now, break the bar at 1970 into a second, visually distinct segment (open or hatched) with its own label, and keep the 1921-1970 chip anchored on the solid segment only.

findings.where: Bottom ledger rail, all shots (verified on d-ch2, d-ch4, d-ch9, d-a3-flood)
findings.what: Every historical ledger entry year (1833, 1893, 1908, 1919, 1927, 1939, 1948, 1958, 1962) is stamped in rust; sampled pixels are ~rgb(163,77,46), which is #A8502F within anti-aliasing.
findings.why: Hard law says rust means present-day only, with exactly two exceptions (the 2026 register caret, the Woodlawn tower cap). Rust on 1833 teaches the visitor the color means 'ledger entry', which destroys the payoff when rust is supposed to snap to 2026 at the finale.
findings.fix: Set historical ledger years in ink/charcoal (match the entry text weight); reserve rust for the 2026 entry and caret only.

findings.what: The HYDE PARK label is clipped mid-word at the plate edge; it renders as 'HYDE P' with the rest cut by the neatline.
findings.why: Clipped type is the fastest unfinished-map tell there is; this is the marquee zoom state the owner asked for.
findings.fix: Per-crop label placement pass. If a label anchor falls within its own text width of the neatline, nudge it inside or suppress it for that camera state.

findings.where: d-a2-register (right pane, rows C and M)
findings.what: The relay connector dropping from the R bar's 1950 end runs straight through the words 'the deed', and its twin grazes 'unenforceable 1948'; two near-parallel verticals cross the C row's annotation zone.
findings.why: The connectors ARE the thesis (the baton pass); a line cutting through its own caption reads as a plotting accident and muddies the one diagram that finally draws the relay.
findings.fix: Give annotations a paper-colored halo the connectors pass behind, or offset the connector x a few pixels so it drops in clear space between the subtitle and the end-note.

findings.what: Footer microcopy reads 'sheets filed through undated sheets. 703 of 703', wrapping as '703 of / 703'.
findings.why: It reads as a template slot filled with a batch name instead of a date; broken visitor-facing copy on the flagship flood beat, and it breaks the historian register.
findings.fix: Special-case the final batch, e.g. 'all 703 sheets filed, the undated batch last', and keep the count on one line.

findings.what: The PLSS section grid is clipped to a data bounding box, not to the land or the neatline. It grids open Lake Michigan on the east and stops at a hard, unexplained bare-cream strip down the entire west side of the plate.
findings.why: The grid is presented as the 1830s survey instrument itself; the 1830s plats did not rule sections across open water, and the arbitrary west edge reads as a clipping bug. Figure-ground breaks on the one beat that is supposed to show the instrument honestly.
findings.fix: Clip the grid to the shoreline (land side only) and extend it to the neatline on the west, or clip to the documented surveyed-township extent and draw that boundary so the edge is explained.

findings.what: Overlay collisions sever four base labels: the $440,000 card hides 'LAKE' leaving an orphaned ' MICHIGAN'; the Woodlawn tower hatch covers 'HYDE' (orphan 'PARK') and 'THE LO'; the Lawndale tower splits 'NORTH ... NDALE'.
findings.why: Label discipline collapses exactly where the exhibit closes its argument; orphaned fragments float next to the towers and read as noise on the most photographed state of the page.
findings.fix: When towers and callout cards are active, suppress the base-map labels they intersect (or relocate LAKE MICHIGAN into open water and drop the neighborhood labels for this state).

findings.what: 'returned after 2008' is an annotation floating in empty space; no bar, tick, or segment is drawn at or after 2008 on the S row.
findings.why: This is the exact 'stated in text but not drawn' failure the R9 audit called out on this same panel; an annotation with no mark undercuts the wall's claim to draw its evidence.
findings.fix: Draw a second S segment from 2008 to the axis end (open/hatched to distinguish it from the 1952-1970 solid bar), bound to the registered fact that sources the return.

findings.what: 'THE RENEWAL PLAN LAY INSIDE THIS TOWNSHIP' floats mid-plate over an unchanged parcel field; nothing is drawn for clearance or the renewal area, and the frame still carries the grade-depth disclosure though no grades are displayed in this state.
findings.why: The R10 brief's own audit flagged 'nothing showing clearance at 1955'; the chapter's one visual claim still has no visual, and a map annotation pointing at nothing reads as a placeholder on the wall.
findings.fix: If a sourceable Hyde Park A/B renewal-area boundary can be digitized from the 1958 plan, draw it dashed with a named source; otherwise demote the sentence to the plate footer as a caption and drop the stale depth disclosure from grade-free states.

findings.what: The lake fill bleeds past the inner neatline at the top-right, and the 1940 stamp sits astride the bled zone outside the frame line.
findings.why: Fill escaping the neatline is a small but classic unfinished-plate tell on the very first image visitors see.
findings.fix: Clip the water polygon to the neatline rect; keep the year stamp in the margin, fully outside the frame.

findings.what: The '1917' stamp is dark-on-dark and its final digit overhangs the sheet corner; the 32 marks and commission square occupy the left third while 60 percent of the plate is empty dim lake.
findings.why: The stamp is near-illegible and half-clipped; the composition wastes the frame. A static, plumb recentring west keeps every memorial law (flat, motionless, undecorated) while giving the marks the wall.
findings.fix: Lighten the stamp or add a halo, keep it inside the corner, and shift the memorial crop west so the marks sit near center; no motion needed.

findings.what: The rust caption 'EAST WOODLAWN, 2026' sits directly on saturated D-red and C-yellow parcels with a weak halo; it shimmers and nearly vanishes.
findings.why: Rust-on-red is the lowest-contrast pairing on the palette, and this caption is the sentence's payoff ('the rust ring at East Woodlawn is 2026').
findings.fix: Strengthen the paper halo, or move the caption into the lake margin with a short leader to the ring.

findings.what: Anachronistic labels on dated plates: THE MIDWAY on the 1833 sheet (the Midway was laid out for 1893) and THE LOOP on the 1832 sheet.
findings.why: The plates present themselves as dated sheets (year stamps, township caption); period-impossible labels undercut the dated-sheet conceit and the historian register.
findings.fix: Either gate labels by era, or style persistent wayfinding labels as clearly modern finding aids (lighter, different face) so they read as annotation, not period content.

findings.where: d-a2-register (map pane), plus docked rail from d-ch0 onward
findings.what: Two orphan cues: an unlabeled small square outline floats under HYDE PARK in the overture map state, and the rail's R/C/M/S/U letter chips appear from chapter 1, a full act before the wall defines them.
findings.why: Unexplained marks and unexplained codes both fail the two-second-stranger test the brief set for the register.
findings.fix: Suppress the today-ring/anchor square until its chapter, and give the rail a one-line key on first appearance (or introduce chips only after the wall names them).

findings.what: The tight commission-square zoom is still captioned CHICAGO, THE SURVEYED CITY (the citywide plate title), and the paired document cards mix date formats ('Filed Jan’40' vs 'Filed November 1, 1939').
findings.why: Plate titles that do not follow the camera, and inconsistent citation formats, are label-discipline slips a museum registrar would catch.
findings.fix: Bind the plate caption to the camera state (e.g. THE COMMISSION SQUARE for the ch5 zoom) and normalize both cards to the long date form.

lens: Exhibition designer with a cartographer's eye (Imhof / NYT graphics desk): composition, ink hierarchy, figure-ground, label discipline, drawn-versus-stated honesty, state by state.
praise: The register wall is now a real annotated Gantt whose baton-pass connectors finally draw the relay instead of asserting it, and the opening plate at last sits in a city (lake, whisper fabric, anchored labels), while the finale's unit-sliver dollar towers with the one rust cap and the sourced colophon are honest spectacle that earns the wall.

findings.what: The flood pull resolves as two camera states, not three. a3-f1 is tight (cam southSide), but a3-f2 sets cam "wide", which is the citywide home crop, and a3-f3 carries that identical camera. d-a3-f2 and d-a3-f3 are pixel-identical framings; the middle station does not exist and the payoff beat ("The map you began with is back") receives no arrival. Keyboard and reduced-motion visitors, who only see resolved states, get two consecutive identical frames during the exhibit's set-piece.
findings.why: Verdict §3 act3 is explicit: "three discrete per-step eases... f1 tight, f2 mid pull, f3 lands citywide exactly as the map completes." The three-ease decomposition was the council's replacement for the killed scroll-spanning pull. Also the owner's directive that the camera track what is discussed: f2's copy is "the sheets keep coming and the map fills", a middle-distance idea shown from maximum distance.
findings.fix: Emit a mid focus box from exhibit-ground-prep.mjs (roughly 2x the southSide box, e.g. the city's south half) as cam "southHalf"; set a3-f2 to it and leave a3-f3 cam "wide" restated so the wide landing coincides with the final batches inking.

findings.where: data/exhibit/ground-copy.json (a3-s1 stage, line ~366) · d-a3-s1.png, d-a3-article34.png, d-a3-deed.png
findings.what: After ch5's push to the bombingField crop, cam persists (carry-forward) through a3-article34, a3-deed, and a3-s1, so the page's tightest zoom sits under a step whose claim is county-wide ("hundreds of Cook County subdivisions carried covenants"). The pull-back then spends itself on ch6's chapter head instead of the step that needed it. d-a3-s1 confirms: the Black Belt dots fill the frame while the text talks about all of Cook County.
findings.why: Owner's directive: the camera zooms into what is discussed. Here it is inverted, discussion widens to the county while the camera stays at maximum zoom for three steps, and it reads as a forgotten camera, not a choice. Restating wide at a3-s1 also lets ch6 arrive with no move (arrive-early spirit).
findings.fix: Add cam: "wide" (and marksMode: "badge" if desired) to a3-s1's stage so the widening claim gets the widening frame; ch6 then arrives static.

findings.what: The second-sheet cut into the Black Belt crop lands ON the memorial beat, not before it. a2-s1 has no stage so it carries ch3's hydePark frame; ch4 itself performs the frame cut plus the dim swap. The settle animation is correctly suppressed by the data-dim rule (globals.css line 1572), so what remains is an instant hard swap plus darkening exactly on ch4's entry, and the suite's arrive-early check evidently does not count frame or dim changes as moves.
findings.why: Verdict §3 act2, binding: "The step before ch4 completes the cut to a recomposed Black Belt crop and settles plumb, so entering the memorial involves zero motion." The registry law (design.md: no cam change lands on ch4) is being satisfied on a technicality because frame is a separate field from cam.
findings.fix: Land frame: "blackBelt" + dim on the step before ch4 (either give a2-s1 that stage or insert a text-light pre-step), leaving ch4's entry with zero state change except the permitted marks reveal; extend the suite's arrive-early assertion to include frame and dim deltas at ch4/a3-s2.

findings.where: data/exhibit/ground-copy.json (ch5 stage, line ~330) · src/lib/exhibit/ground/types.ts (VeilTarget, line 25) · src/lib/exhibit/ground/geometry.json
findings.what: The verdict's ch5 spotlight ("veil on Binga's block") does not exist anywhere in the build. VeilTarget has no binga entry, geometry.json's veilHoles are only jacksonPark/jacksonParkHp/lawndale/township/woodlawn, and ch5's stage sets no veil. design.md engineering decision 3 claims the prep script emits a "binga block" hole; it does not. The camera arrives close and the dots resolve, but nothing is singled out, and the deviation is recorded nowhere.
findings.why: Verdict §3 act3 specifies the veil on Binga's block as part of the semantic-zoom arrival; the veil is what turns "a cloud of dots" into "this man's block, hit again and again." Silent deviations from the binding plan are exactly what the audit loop exists to catch.
findings.fix: Emit a bingaBlock hole in exhibit-ground-prep.mjs from the already-geocoded Binga bombing rows (real geometry only), add it to VeilTarget and ch5's stage; if the block geometry can't be honestly derived, record the omission in design.md like the streets/renewal gates.

findings.what: Towers mount at a6-bridge, the same instant the sheet begins its 0-to-22deg lean. The sheet's rotateX transitions over 700ms, but .gtower's counter-rotation reads var(--gtilt) statically and has no transform transition, so for the length of the lean the towers stand at the full -22deg against a sheet that is mid-flight: they shear backward and snap perpendicular only when the lean settles. Same for the counter-rotated legend chip. This artifact plays on the finale's marquee 3D beat.
findings.why: The 3D grammar's one promise is that dollars stand truly perpendicular to the sheet (verdict §2, "no in-plane fake axonometry"); during the lean that promise visibly breaks. Verdict also says towers hide during tweens, and the tilt transition is a tween the data-tween flag does not cover.
findings.fix: Give .gtower (and the legend chip) transition: transform 700ms cubic-bezier(0.22,1,0.36,1) to match .ground-sheet exactly, so sheet and counter-rotation track each other through the lean; reduced motion already resolves instantly.

findings.what: Mid-track, the climb frames almost nothing: the white-median column's fill (#F7F1E3) is near-identical to the page linen, so the multi-viewport track renders as two 1px border hairlines with empty interior (d-a6-climb shows a viewport of whitespace, one waypoint caption, and the minimap). The black bar has ended above the fold, so the thing whose height IS the argument reads as an empty outline for roughly four viewports.
findings.why: Owner ordered faster-reading charts and less boring; verdict §3 stages the climb as "one pressed bar against one rising stack." A stack that renders as an untinted void is a camera position framing nothing, page after page.
findings.fix: Fill the white column with the towers' SLIVER_STACK repeating gradient (one sliver = a disclosed dollar amount, same act6 material grammar) or at minimum a visibly deeper paper tone; the mid-climb viewports then always contain countable material.

findings.what: The finale copy and sr both point the visitor at "the township line" on the one-map read, but the citywide boundary ghost is a ~16x13 screen-pixel rectangle (path bbox 52x38 viewBox units at the home crop) drawn at 50% ink under the D fills, the marks cluster, and immediately abutting the rust ring; in the shot it is effectively unfindable. Its footprint also looks several times smaller than the township polygon the visitor spent acts 1-4 on (the hp sheet's boundary spans Washington Park to the lake), so the label may be naming the wrong geometry.
findings.why: "Every map checked" and the historian register: closing copy directs attention to a feature that cannot carry the read, and possibly to a different polygon than the one it names. The one-map read is the exhibit's last argument.
findings.fix: Verify which real polygon the ghost is (township vs Hyde Park-Kenwood); if it is not the township, redraw from the hp boundary's source geometry projected to citywide, and give it the boundary treatment used on the hp sheet (heavier ink, above the fills) so the closing sentence lands.

findings.what: The filing counter ends on "sheets filed through undated sheets. 703 of 703", broken register ("filed through undated sheets") at the flood's payoff, and it counts 703 "sheets" while the GradeFlood panel in the same viewport says "ACROSS ALL 576 SHEETS" (d-a3-flood shows both simultaneously). 703 is the inked-area count, not a sheet count; the noun is wrong on one of the two claims.
findings.why: Real-data law: two conflicting sheet totals visible at once reads as a caught error; the counter is title-block furniture the camera plan itself specifies as ticking "through the real sheet dates."
findings.fix: Change the counter noun to areas ("areas graded ... 703 of 703") and make the final label a real date with undated sheets handled separately (e.g. "through Apr 1940, plus undated sheets").

findings.what: ch1's sr-only sentence tells non-visual visitors the plat leans up "with the survey's section lines, the shoreline, and the township boundary", but the same stage sets boundary: false and d-ch1 shows no boundary. The verdict's ch1 ground stack also lists the township boundary as part of tilt event one.
findings.why: Non-visual parity is the council's stated law (each step's sr states the resolved state); as shipped the sr asserts a stratum that is hidden. Cheap to fix, and it is a screen-reader lie on the first camera event of the walk.
findings.fix: Set boundary: true at ch1 (matching the verdict's ground stack) or strike "and the township boundary" from the sr; do the matching suite assertion so sr and resolved state can't diverge again.

findings.what: The verdict's 1893 beat ("the camera pushes 20 percent tighter as Jackson Park, Washington Park, and the Midway print") is not implemented; resolveBox only honors named focus targets when frame === citywide, so the entire hydePark sheet has no camera capability and ch1/ch2/a1-fair are the same static home crop. The deviation is not recorded in design.md's engineering decisions.
findings.why: A binding act-plan move dropped silently; act1 is also where the owner's "less boring" complaint bites hardest since the township sheet holds one framing for six steps.
findings.fix: Extend resolveBox to accept focus boxes in hydePark coordinates (the prep script already emits hp-frame layers; add an hpFocus map) and give ch2/a1-fair the 20 percent push; or record the cut in design.md alongside the streets/renewal gates.

findings.what: The fresh evidence set has no shot of a3-f1 at either width, and the scenario suite asserts only the filing counter there, not the camera, so the flood's one tight state (and the only within-frame zoom in the flood) ships with no visual evidence and no CameraState assertion; a regressed or missing southSide focus would pass silently.
findings.why: The verify contract in the verdict promises resolved CameraState per step, all 54, both widths; the flood's camera is exactly where R10's new machinery lives.
findings.fix: Add a3-f1 to the shot list and assert its resolved viewBox width (< ~60 percent of home) alongside the counter assertion.

findings.what: At the bombingField camera the HYDE PARK label is clipped mid-word by the pane edge ("HYDE P"). Labels counter-scale with --gtext-k but are never culled or faded when their anchor sits at or beyond the crop boundary, so close cameras can slice type.
findings.why: "Every map checked": a chopped word at the exhibit's most-repeated close camera reads as a rendering bug and it sits on screen for four consecutive steps.
findings.fix: Give city labels a per-focus visibility gate (hide labels whose anchor falls outside the target box inflated by ~10 percent) via a data attribute the controller already has the numbers to set.

findings.what: The 1833 plat prints THE MIDWAY (an 1893 fairground landscape) and the modern HYDE PARK display name on a sheet whose strata table exists specifically to refuse faked period detail before 1893; the hp label layer is not era-gated the way fabric and parks are.
findings.why: The ground-plane table's own rationale ("no community fabric; it is a modern index and would fake period detail") applies with equal force to an anachronistic label on the survey's oldest instrument; historian register.
findings.fix: Era-gate the hp label layer like parks (THE MIDWAY from 1893 on; optionally hold HYDE PARK until the 1853 Cornell beat), one strataFor field plus one CSS rule.

lens: Title-design cinematographer: camera choreography, 3D grammar, and whether each staged move lands where the verdict says it must
praise: The core grammar is genuinely disciplined: the destination-first FLIP camera with computed-matrix retargeting is textbook, tilt stays a three-event scarcity with the memorial hard-frozen (the data-dim settle suppression is a lovely catch), press is resolver-monotonic and measurably present, and the counter-rotated, --gsv-registered towers with the disclosed sliver legend are exactly the honest 3D the council ordered.

lens: Conservator and historian of racial-violence exhibitions: memorial dignity, real-data provenance, pigment law, register truth against machines.json, sr-sentence parity, disclosure wording

findings.where: src/app/globals.css:847 (.ground-ledger-rail .glr-year), evidence in d-ch4.png, m-ch4.png, d-a3-f3.png, d-a2-register.png
findings.what: The fixed ledger rail prints EVERY posted entry's year in rust: 1833, 1893, 1908 (visible in rust on the memorial screen itself), 1927, 1939, 1962. The rail comment claims 'Rust because rust means now', but these years are not now. R10 re-inked the register caret from rust to ink for exactly this reason and left the rail untouched.
findings.why: Breaks the hard pigment law: rust means present-day only, with two enumerated exceptions (register caret at 2026, Woodlawn tower cap). The rail is on screen at every step, including ch4.
findings.fix: In globals.css change .glr-year to var(--color-exh-ink); allow rust only when the posted entry is closing-totals (year 2026), e.g. a [data-now="on"] attribute set in LedgerRail.tsx when latest.year >= 2026. Mirror in the suite.

findings.what: The on-sheet honesty line reads 'Depth shows grade rank in four equal steps' but the drawn depths are 0.6 / 1.1 / 1.7 / 2.4, increments of 0.5, 0.6, 0.7, which are not equal steps (the ink opacity ladder 0.16 + 0.09*d is unequal too). The exhibit's one disclosure misdescribes its own drawing.
findings.why: The disclosure is the R7/R10 honesty instrument; a false word inside it undermines the real-data covenant. The a3-s2 sr sentence ('four ranked steps') is the accurate wording.
findings.fix: Either change PRESS_DEPTH to a true equal ladder (0.6 / 1.2 / 1.8 / 2.4, visually indistinguishable) or drop 'equal' from the disclosure ('four ranked steps'). Suite only asserts includes('Depth shows grade rank'), so both are safe.

findings.what: Below 1024px the rank disclosure is display:none while the intaglio press still applies, so every phone visitor gets the depth encoding with no disclosure ever printed. m-a3-s2.png shows the pressed map with only 'CHICAGO, THE SURVEYED CITY' in the title block.
findings.why: Breaks the R7 ruling that the quantized-rank depth ships WITH an on-page disclosure, and the parity law (phone = identical resolved states). An entire device class loses the honesty line.
findings.fix: Remove the display:none; keep the line at reduced size (it already fits: 210px max-width, 9px type wraps to three short lines) or move it into the mobile tap sheet, but it must print somewhere on-page at data-press="on".

findings.where: public/exhibit-data/hp-frame-layers.json (sources.boundaryAndLabels) vs StageController.tsx:55 (FRAME_LABEL 'HYDE PARK TOWNSHIP'), ground-copy.json ch1 sr, a4 note ('The renewal plan lay inside this township'), a6-sum text and sr ('The township line marks where the walk began')
findings.what: The boundary the exhibit repeatedly calls 'the township' is, per its own source record, the modern Hyde Park COMMUNITY-AREA boundary (about 1.7 x 1.25 miles at map scale). The historic Hyde Park Township of 1861-1889 ran from 39th to 138th Street, State Street to the lake, roughly thirty times larger. The chapter frame itself is titled 'The first taking, 1832 to 1889', so the copy unambiguously means the historic township.
findings.why: Historian-register accuracy and the real-data rule: the layer is real but mislabeled as a different, much larger historical entity; on the 1833 plat it is also an anachronism (the community area is a 20th-century statistical unit).
findings.fix: Smallest fix is wording: frame plate 'HYDE PARK' (drop TOWNSHIP), a6-sum 'The Hyde Park line marks where the walk began', a4 note 'inside this neighborhood'. Larger fix: source the real township polygon and draw it. Either way, name the community-area boundary as such in the colophon ground-sources paragraph.

findings.where: data/exhibit/ground-copy.json a3-f1 (sr + cam southSide) against geometry.json floodOrder; no d-/m-a3-f1 screenshot exists to have caught it
findings.what: The a3-f1 sr claims 'The first filed sheets ink the South Side while the camera sits close', but zero of the 35 September 1939 areas fall inside the southSide focus box; 13 of 35 are on the North Side entirely, and at common pane aspects only 8-17 of 35 ink inside the padded frame. Most of the flood's opening event happens off-screen.
findings.why: The sr sentence states a drawn fact that is not drawn (sr parity law), and it defeats the owner's R10 directive that the camera zooms into what is discussed.
findings.fix: Either keep cam wide at a3-f1 and reword the sr to 'The first filed sheets ink across the map', or emit a real focus box around the Sep 1939 batch's extent in exhibit-ground-prep.mjs and aim the camera there. Then add the missing a3-f1 shots.

findings.where: src/components/exhibit/ground/StageController.tsx:336-338 (filing counter) vs Colophon.tsx sheetTotal (576), evidence d-a3-f3.png; suite locks the wording at scripts/exhibit-scenarios.mjs:389
findings.what: The filing counter calls all 703 flood ids 'sheets' ('sheets filed through undated sheets. 703 of 703' at a3-f3), while the colophon door on the same page says 'All 576 surveyors' sheets, searchable'. 576 is the true sheet count (532 dated + 44 undated); 127 graded areas have no surviving sheet, and 9 flood ids (1060-1068) have no drawn path at all so nothing inks for them. The final label 'filed through undated sheets' is also broken syntax.
findings.why: Real-data precision on a visible instrument: the exhibit asserts 703 sheets exist twice per flood and contradicts its own study-room count. The suite currently enforces the wrong words.
findings.fix: Change the counter to count what it counts: 'areas graded ... N of 703' (or 694 drawn areas after reconciling the 9 phantom ids), and give the last batch a truthful label ('undated and sheetless areas'). Update exhibit-scenarios.mjs:389 in the same commit.

findings.where: data/exhibit/ground-copy.json ch1 stage (sr vs boundary:false), evidence d-ch1.png
findings.what: The ch1 sr tells screen-reader visitors the 1833 plat shows 'the survey's section lines, the shoreline, and the township boundary', but the same stage sets boundary:false and CSS hides [data-hp-boundary]; d-ch1.png confirms no boundary is drawn. The boundary first appears at a1-s2.
findings.why: sr sentences are the non-visual parity contract; this one asserts a drawn state that is not drawn (and an 1861 boundary on an 1833 plat would be anachronistic anyway).
findings.fix: Drop 'and the township boundary' from the ch1 sr (keep the boundary's true first appearance at a1-s2, where the sr can mention it).

findings.where: .r9shots/ (6 steps missing at both widths: a0-r2, a1-s2, a3-f1, a3-takeaway, a4-takeaway, a5-takeaway)
findings.what: The audit evidence set covers 54 of 60 resolved steps. Among the missing are stage-changing states: a0-r2 (bare-ground state), a1-s2 (boundary turns on), a3-f1 (the flood's first ink, where the camera/sr defect above sits), and a5-takeaway (the green CBL credit posts).
findings.why: The R10 contract is fresh screenshots of every step at 1280 and 390; the holes fall exactly where two of this review's defects live.
findings.fix: Extend scripts/exhibit-shots.mjs to enumerate step ids from ground-copy.json rather than a hand list, so a missing shot fails the run.

findings.where: StageBase.tsx today tag + LedgerColumn.tsx DollarTowers, evidence d-a6-ledger.png
findings.what: During the act6 money beats the Woodlawn deed stack plants directly over the rust ring and the 'EAST WOODLAWN, 2026' tag, and the rust type (#A8502F) sits on full-strength D-grade red (#B0322B), so the exhibit's one present-day map mark is nearly illegible exactly when the finale discusses it.
findings.why: Hurts the finale's read of the one rust mark the pigment law protects; the label halo does not rescue rust-on-red contrast.
findings.fix: Offset the tower base a few viewBox units from the ring (or shift the tag below the tower footprint) and thicken the linen halo on [data-today-tag] so rust never sits directly on D red.

findings.where: InstrumentRegister.tsx RegisterWall end notes, evidence d-a2-register.png
findings.what: The 'unenforceable 1948' end note collides with the 'the deed' alias text on the Restrictive covenants row (both render at the same line height around the 1948 x-position).
findings.why: Legibility on the thesis wall; the dated court-defeat annotations are part of the register's evidence read.
findings.fix: Give .gr-wall-endnote a slightly higher top offset or nudge the alias into the label column's own line so the two never share a baseline.

findings.where: LedgerColumn.tsx DeedTower place="Lawndale" vs map label, ledger rows, and the towers' sr sentence
findings.what: The tower plate reads 'LAWNDALE' while the map label, the ledger entries, and the sr sentence all say North Lawndale, which is where the anchor actually sits and what the Duke study covers.
findings.why: Register consistency: the fact is about North Lawndale contract buyers; 'Lawndale' names a different, larger area.
findings.fix: Change place to 'North Lawndale' (the plate width tolerates it; keep the -44% plate shift).

praise: The memorial discipline is genuinely museum-grade: the dim+sheetcut animation suppression, the suite-enforced boundary seal, all 32 placed marks verified inside the crop, and a docket that counts and refuses to name, while the rebuilt register derives every bar, baton, and the union band from machines.json with a guard that makes a false handoff undrawable.

lens: Fresh visitor on a 390px phone, 90 seconds, two-second reads; parity checked against d-ch0 and d-a6-climb. Note for the suite: the requested shot m-a3-f1 does not exist in .r9shots (set has m-a3-f2/f3; I reviewed those).

findings.what: The Woodlawn tower cap plate is clipped by the viewport top for the entire act-6 finale on mobile. The headline figure $440,000 shows only the bottom half of its digits, and the plate also crowds the 2026 era readout. This is the resolved state across three consecutive beats, not a transient.
findings.why: Materially hurts the visit at its climax. The one sanctioned rust tower cap, the number the whole exhibit builds to, never reads on a phone, and this would be THE screenshot-a-friend moment. Also strains the phone-equals-desktop resolved-state law, since d-a6-climb shows the full plate.
findings.fix: At the phone breakpoint clamp the deed-stack height or scale (or pan the act-6 camera south a few viewBox units) so the Woodlawn cap plate resolves fully inside the sticky stage frame below the era readout.

findings.where: m-ch2, m-ch4, m-ch5, m-a3-f2, m-a3-s2, m-ch9, m-a6-bridge (ledger strip on every mobile viewport)
findings.what: The docked ledger strip prints historical entry years in rust: 1833, 1893, 1908, 1919, 1927, 1939, 1962, 1971 all sample at #A8502F, the exh-rust token (rule is .ground-ledger-rail .glr-year in src/app/globals.css line 847).
findings.why: Breaks the hard law that rust means present-day only, whose stated exceptions are the register caret at 2026 and the Woodlawn tower cap. The register itself keeps its caret ink until 2026, so the page chrome contradicts its own color grammar on every screen.
findings.fix: Set .glr-year to ink, keeping rust only when the posted entry year is 2026 (data-now style, same pattern as the register caret).

findings.what: Mobile chapter-boundary resolved states waste the screen. At ch0 the text begins mid-sentence ("neighborhoods for mortgage lenders, A down to D...") with the exhibit title scrolled off, while d-ch0 shows the full title and intro. At ch1, ch4, ch5, ch9 roughly half the viewport is blank cream with the chapter kicker pinned at the very bottom edge.
findings.why: A 90-second phone visitor repeatedly meets a subject-less clause or a near-empty screen; keyboard and reduced-motion users who step to these anchors land on exactly these states, so the resolved-state guarantee serves emptiness. (If an archival image is supposed to fill the ch4/ch5 gap, it had not rendered at capture time, which is worth checking separately.)
findings.fix: Retune mobile step anchoring and pre-chapter spacers so each chapter resolves with the kicker and heading in the upper half beneath the dock, and ch0 resolves at the top of the title block.

findings.what: The fixed ledger N button sits directly on top of the REPORTED source-status chip under the $440,000 sentence; only "...ORTED" peeks out.
findings.why: That chip is the real-data disclosure for a press-reported figure, and act 6 is exactly where a skeptical visitor checks sourcing. Occluding it undercuts the every-figure-names-its-source promise on phones.
findings.fix: Add bottom clearance (padding equal to the N button diameter plus margin) to the steps pane at the phone breakpoint, or render source chips inline at the end of the sentence instead of on their own bottom-left line.

findings.what: The required sliver legend ("One sliver is $10,000, dollars as noted") overlaps the CHICAGO, THE SURVEYED CITY stage label at 390px, covering its last letters.
findings.why: Two pieces of stage chrome colliding in the flagship scene reads as a bug and dents the pressed-sheet craft; the legend is a mandated disclosure and deserves clean placement.
findings.fix: At narrow widths stack the legend on its own line above the stage label or right-align it flush to the frame edge clear of the label.

findings.what: Story years before 1900 (1832, 1833, 1893) clamp the caret to the left end of the 1900-2026 rail, so three different years occupy the same position over the 1900 tick.
findings.why: The instrument quietly lies about position in its first three appearances, the moment a stranger is deciding whether the strip is trustworthy or decorative.
findings.fix: When the story year predates the rail, hide the caret tick and show the year chip alone flush left (or add a small off-scale notch left of the 1900 tick).

findings.what: The mobile dock gives no visible affordance that tapping opens the five-lane instrument sheet; it reads as a static graphic, and the union band label at 390px renders around 6px.
findings.why: The verdict's mobile design depends on tap-to-open for the five instruments; without a hint, the stranger never meets RULE/DEED/MAP/BULLDOZER/CONTRACT on a phone, so the bottom strip stays half-meaningful.
findings.fix: Add a subtle chevron or FIVE INSTRUMENTS tap hint at the right end of the dock strip on phones.

findings.what: At 390px the end-cap court phrases ("written out 1950", "unenforceable 1948") wrap into orphan lines floating between the lane name and its bar, right-indented to nothing in particular.
findings.why: The wall is the exhibit's argument-in-one-figure; orphaned annotations read as layout accidents and slow the two-second lane read.
findings.fix: At the phone breakpoint give end-cap phrases their own right-aligned line tied under the bar's end (with the date range), instead of letting them wrap off the name line.

findings.what: Entry 11 copy differs by platform: mobile strip reads "The bill still outstanding", desktop reads "The century's bill, still outstanding".
findings.why: Same entry, two texts; a small crack in the one-experience parity promise and in the record-reads-exactly discipline.
findings.fix: Pick one string for entry 11 and use it at both breakpoints.

findings.what: The panel text says "the rust ring at East Woodlawn is 2026", but at 390px the ring is a 3-4px fleck and the EAST WOODLAWN, 2026 label that desktop shows is illegible or absent.
findings.why: The summation asks the visitor to find something the phone rendering cannot show, ending the read on a broken pointer.
findings.fix: Scale the rust ring (and its small label) up at the phone breakpoint for a6-sum, or have the camera favor the South Side in that resolved frame.

praise: The pinned sheet with its era chip, the wet-ink ledger strip counting Entry n of 11, and the full ledger wall at m-a6-ledger all read instantly at 390px, and the Lawndale $71,000 plate is dead legible; the phone visit has a real spine.

lens: Ruthless creative technologist. R10 engine correctness and performance, reviewed at HEAD (45314bc) and verified live: headless-Chrome probes of mid-flight camera frames, money-beat resize, deep links, fast-scroll flood, plus pixel inspection of the shipped screenshots.

findings.what: The intaglio filter is inverted. feComposite in="blur" in2="SourceAlpha" operator="out" keeps the blurred offset OUTSIDE the shape, painting a dark fringe along the bottom-right OUTER edges of every graded fill. Confirmed by zooming d-a3-s2.png: shadow outside lower-right edges, top-left edges clean. That is a drop shadow; the grade fills read as plates RAISED off the paper.
findings.why: Inverts the binding R10 language (council-verdict/design.md): policy presses DOWN into the paper, only true dollars rise UP. As shipped, graded areas visually rise, which is the register reserved for the dollar towers. Also the ink spills outside each fill onto neighboring ground.
findings.fix: Swap the operands: <feComposite in="SourceAlpha" in2="blur" operator="out"/> so the ink lands inside the top-left inner edge of each fill (classic inner shadow), then re-shoot a3-s2 and eyeball a D area against a raised control.

findings.where: src/components/exhibit/ground/engine/camera.ts go() (destination-first FLIP on the svg element)
findings.what: Every within-frame zoom-IN starts with a hard cut that deletes the rest of the city. Measured live at a2-takeaway -> ch5: at flight start the svg carries transform matrix(~0.105) with the new viewBox, and svg element clipping discards everything outside the destination crop; the captured frame (flight-1-early.png) is blank linen with a small floating postcard that then grows. Labels simultaneously pop to ~1/4 size (HYDE PARK label 80.25px -> 18.6px in 80ms) because --gtext-k applies at t=0.
findings.why: Directly defeats the owner's order (camera zooms into what is discussed, 3D married to the 2D map) and the engine's own comment that the picture never jumps. It reads as a slide swap, not a camera move, twice per visit (ch5, a3-f1).
findings.fix: FLIP an inner <g> wrapper instead of the svg element: set the destination viewBox, apply the inverse transform to the group, transition the group to identity. Content outside the viewBox keeps drawing inside the fixed svg viewport, so the wide context stays on screen through the whole flight and clipping stays at the sheet edge. Defer the --gtext-k/--gsv writes to transitionend (or tween them) so labels and pinned HTML do not snap at t=0.

findings.what: Every zoom-OUT paints the flying map over the entire page. Measured at a3-f1 -> a3-f2, 120ms in: the transformed svg box is 1282x1448px at x=-507,y=-409 versus the 579x654 sheet; the captured frame shows the lake and grade fills covering the desk, the pane border, and the reading column text for most of the 900ms tween (both zoom-outs: a3-s1 -> ch6 and a3-f1 -> a3-f2).
findings.why: Breaks the desk/sheet metaphor the whole R10 design hangs on, and makes the step text unreadable mid-flight; also a giant upscaled raster each flight (the wide render scaled 9.5x) which is the worst case for the 55fps perf gate.
findings.fix: Same inner-group FLIP as the zoom-in fix resolves it structurally (clip stays at the svg viewport). If the element-level FLIP must stay for a hotfix, add overflow:hidden (or clip-path) to .ground-sheet, which contains the spill but still leaves the zoom-in vanish.

findings.what: The suite cannot catch any of the above and misses the new surfaces. (a) The press check only asserts getComputedStyle(filter).includes("url"), so the inverted emboss shipped green; assert the filter's operand order or sample a pressed edge. (b) Every scenario waits 1300ms+ before reading, so no mid-flight frame is ever observed and both P1 camera defects are invisible; add one probe that screenshots ~150ms into the ch5 tween and asserts map coverage outside the focus box and svg bounds within the sheet. (c) Zero coverage of the act6 towers: no gtower presence at money beats, no tower-base-vs-rust-ring alignment, no rust-cap-only-on-Woodlawn, no legend, no exh-green-only-on-CBL. (d) No resize scenario, so the new ResizeObserver re-derivation (45314bc) ships untested. (e) design.md says the arrive-early law (no cam change lands on a solemn chapterHead or a3-s2/ch4) is 'checked by the suite'; no such data-shape check exists. (f) The reduced-motion scenario stops at the flood; it never asserts tilt/press/veil resolve identically. (g) The mobile scenario never asserts the 8deg tilt cap or the under-480 band-only dock. (h) Nothing measures the design's binding 55fps tween gate.
findings.why: The verify suite is the only regression net for laws the owner made binding (press direction, rust register, reduced-motion parity), and it just demonstrably let the central metaphor ship inverted.
findings.fix: Extend ground-pressed-sheet with: feComposite operand assertion, one mid-tween frame assertion, a money-beat block (tower presence, ring alignment within 2px, one rust cap, legend text), a viewport-resize re-derivation check, the arrive-early data-shape lint over RESOLVED_STEPS, and tilt/press/veil assertions inside ground-motion and ground-mobile.

findings.what: Camera-anchored HTML jumps to its destination position at flight start. applyDerived writes --gsv-*/--gtext-k synchronously with the viewBox swap, and only the towers are hidden behind data-tween; the marks badge and the stage note are not. On the ch5 -> ch6 zoom-out the '32 bombed sites' chip mounts pinned to the settled wide-crop coordinates and floats detached from the dot field it counts for the full 900ms while the map slides beneath it.
findings.why: A counted claim visibly detached from the marks it counts undercuts the map-honesty rule (every drawn claim tied to real geography) and looks broken on the one flight most visitors will watch closely.
findings.fix: Hide .ground-marks-badge and .ground-note behind .ground-stage[data-tween="on"] exactly like .ground-towers (two CSS selectors), or defer applyDerived until the camera settles.

findings.where: src/components/exhibit/ground/ (whole R10 surface); no Safari evidence in .r9shots
findings.what: No Safari or iOS Safari pass exists, and R10 stacks WebKit's three flakiest features on one element chain: CSS transform transitions on the svg root read back via getComputedStyle mid-flight (the retarget math depends on it), SVG url() filters over full-city union paths inside a preserve-3d rotated ancestor (press + tilt 22 across all of act6), and vector-effect non-scaling-stroke under CSS transforms. WebKit is known to mis-rasterize or drop filters inside 3D contexts. All fresh shots are headless Chrome at 1280/390.
findings.why: A museum exhibit on a public URL will see heavy iPhone traffic; if WebKit drops the press filters or mis-reads the mid-flight matrix, act3 onward degrades or retargeting snaps, and nothing in the pipeline would notice.
findings.fix: One manual Safari + iOS Safari walk of ch1, ch5, a3-s2, and act6 before ship; wire the design's own pre-built offset-stroke deboss fallback behind a capability/UA check if the filters misbehave, and record the pass in the build state.

findings.what: The label counter-scale divides widths (to.w/home.w) but the home crop is height-constrained under the meet fit, so close cameras oversize type by the letterbox factor: the same label measured 80.25px wide at the home crop and 115.7px settled at ch5 (44% larger), when the stated goal is constant apparent size.
findings.why: Contradicts the code's own contract (type keeps its apparent size) and makes close crops shout slightly, against the historian register.
findings.fix: Compute gtext-k from the meet scales: kHome/kTo where each k = min(paneW/box.w, paneH/box.h), not from the width ratio.

findings.what: The page HTML is 1.07MB (271KB gzipped) because the StageBase subtree is serialized twice, once as markup and again in the RSC flight payload (a distinctive lake fragment appears 4x: two markup uses times two serializations; flight chars ~482KB), and data-fabric/data-lake-lines re-emit full d strings that <use href> could share.
findings.why: Initial payload is the whole budget on the phones this exhibit targets; the duplication is silent and will grow with every geometry addition.
findings.fix: Short term: swap the duplicate fill/pattern paths to <use> references. Longer: restructure so the svg is rendered by a server component that is a sibling of (not a prop into) the client controller, or accept and document the 2x cost with a size gate in the suite.

findings.where: src/app/globals.css R10 block + StageController veil effect + LedgerColumn portal
findings.what: Three small pops and one unsound pattern: (a) a frame cut into a tilted state (ch1) plays ground-sheet-arrive at the full new tilt for 300ms then hands back to the 700ms transform transition mid-flight, a ~1deg backward jump; (b) veil -> "none" clears the hole's d immediately so the veil pops off instead of using its 450ms fade (set fill-opacity first, clear d after); (c) towers pop back in after a tween because the opacity rule targets .ground-towers while the transition lives on .gtower; (d) DollarTowers reads towersSlot.current during render (LedgerColumn.tsx ~193), which only works because activeStep changes force re-renders after the ref attaches; under StrictMode/concurrent rendering or any future StageController remount the portal targets a detached node.
findings.why: (a-c) chip at the one-event-at-a-time cut grammar the verdict specifies; (d) is a latent portal-lifecycle bug waiting for a refactor to expose it.
findings.fix: (a) suppress the transform transition while data-sheetcut is on; (b) reorder the veil writes; (c) move the transition to .ground-towers; (d) hold the slot in state via a callback ref (setSlot) instead of a mutable ref read during render.

praise: The engine's architecture genuinely holds under abuse: the mid-flight retarget math (composing against the live computed matrix) is correct, the resolved-per-step state survived fast-scroll, reverse entry into the flood (exactly 291 of 703 with a truthful filing counter, zero console errors), and a cold deep link into a money beat (towers up, tilt 22, press held), and the ResizeObserver re-derivation added in 45314bc verifiably keeps the towers on the rust ring within 0.2px across resizes.
